system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (Buyer)
**Status:** Internal and privileged. Not for circulation to the Seller.

---

## 1. Headline view

The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced." Read together, the cover note and the Disclosure Letter would:

- cut our recourse sharply, through a lower cap, a 5x higher de minimis, a 5x higher basket that is excess-only, and a shorter claims period;
- fold Title, Capacity, Tax and IP into that reduced regime through a catch-all clause;
- extend the caps, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions to fraud;
- give the Seller a near-total defence through whole-data-room disclosure plus a constructive buyer-knowledge bar;
- leave three cash and completion items unresolved: the Bluefen consent, the Riverlark payout and release, and the AUD 420,000 bonuses.

Several statements in the Seller's cover note are **contradicted by the Seller's own Disclosure Letter**. These should be called out directly, as they undermine the "addressed" and "settled" framing.

**Staleness warning.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026. Every factual position below needs a refreshed source check before we rely on it, including the Riverlark balance, Bluefen status, the DD-006 investigation, Ironquay payment status and the bonus triggers.

---

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis

### A. Liability regime

| # | Issue | Seller position | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | General cap (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m start. 20% is a fallback only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft. | **Reject.** The figure happens to match our fallback, but no authority has been given. A matching number does not clear the term, because the cap's real value depends on what sits beneath it (see A2 to A5 and B1 to B3). Restate 25%. Do not signal the fallback. |
| A2 | De minimis (cl 12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | **Reject.** At 5x our position, many real warranty breaches would be screened out individually. |
| A3 | Basket (cl 12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, first-dollar (tipping) | **Reject both elements.** The excess-only structure permanently forfeits AUD 250,000. A tipping basket at AUD 50,000 is our position. |
| A4 | General claims period (cl 12.3) | 18 months | 24 months. 18 is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's approval (none given). | **Reject.** Restate 24 months. The same authority point as A1 applies. |
| A5 | "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13) | Catch-all | Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate. No hidden general-regime override. | **Reject outright.** This is the most dangerous drafting point. It silently imports the general cap, thresholds and time limit into indemnities, covenants, price and payment obligations, Title, Tax and IP. Reverse the default: general limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated. |

### B. Fundamental, fraud and reliance

| # | Issue | Seller position | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | Title and capacity under the general regime | Same caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | **Reject.** Title is the thing we are buying. A 20% cap on title would mean we could pay AUD 24m and recover at most AUD 4.8m if the shares were not the Seller's to sell. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. |
| B2 | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) | Covers fraud | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of everything, to the maximum extent enforceable. Non-waivable. | **Reject. Non-negotiable.** Insert an express carve-out from all caps, baskets, de minimis, time limits, exclusive-remedy, non-reliance and disclosure and knowledge qualifiers. The carve-out should cover fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct by the Seller, its officers, employees, agents and advisers. Courts may limit reliance on such clauses in fraud cases, and statutory misleading-conduct protections may not be excludable. We should still not rely on that. Draft it expressly. No one on the team has authority to concede this. |
| B3 | Tax and IP "settled under the general regime" | Asserted as settled | Tax and IP remain **OPEN**. Assume neither unlimited liability nor resolution. | **Reject the characterisation.** Nothing has been agreed. Respond that the Tax and IP regimes remain open and subject to separate negotiation. Do not let a "settled" label stand unanswered in correspondence. |

### C. Disclosure and knowledge

| # | Issue | Seller position | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | General disclosure (DL 1.1, 1.2) | The entire data room as at 22 Sep 2026, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records | Specific fair disclosure only. Reject data-room, register and search deemed disclosure. | **Reject 1.1 and 1.2.** Only matters fairly disclosed with sufficient detail for the Buyer to identify their nature and scope should qualify the warranties. Specific disclosures (DL 2 to 10) can stand as specific, subject to the comments below. |
| C2 | DL 1.4 non-admission | Nothing admits breach, consent requirement, and so on | n/a | **Acceptable in principle**, but it must not dilute specific disclosures or operate as a further qualifier. Confirm it does not override the specific statements in DL 2 to 10. |
| C3 | Buyer knowledge bar (cl 8.3) | No claim for anything the Buyer **or its advisers** knew, **including anything discoverable** from the data room or public records | Delete blanket exclusions. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry. Never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. | **Delete.** As drafted it is constructive knowledge imputed through advisers, which effectively voids the warranties. It would also defeat the specific indemnities we need precisely because we know of issues such as Ironquay and DD-006. Note that the playbook's knowledge-persons requirement concerns Seller-awareness qualifiers. Do not offer a "limited" buyer-knowledge clause as a compromise without authority. |

### D. Completion mechanics and cash items

**D1. Bluefen (cl 3/6.3): material departure, plus an internal contradiction**

- The cover note says the consent is "addressed." DL 2 says no final written consent and **no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied** has been provided.
- Bluefen accounts for ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m). Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a customer of that size.
- "Satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" is consent-on-delivery. It ignores the cl 11.3 conditions.
- **Push back:** make it a Condition Precedent requiring (i) effective, unconditional consent in agreed form, or a consent whose conditions are **evidenced as satisfied** before Completion, and (ii) a stronger Seller obligation than reasonable endeavours. Non-satisfaction should not be waivable by the Seller.

**D2. Riverlark (cl 2/7): material departure**

- The facility is "approximately" AUD 3.2m outstanding. DL 3 says it has not been repaid and no discharge exists. A post-Completion release is proposed.
- On a debt-free basis we need: a current payout letter as at the Completion date, including interest, breaks and fees; direct repayment from Completion funds in the funds flow; and executed security releases (including any PPSR registrations) delivered at Completion.
- The change-of-control trigger in DD-003 cl 8.1 heightens the risk.
- A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable payout and release undertaking from the bank **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither is in place.
- **Reject** the current wording.

**D3. Employee bonuses (DD-005): silent exclusion**

- The funds flow omits AUD 420,000 in Completion bonuses. The Seller says they are "a matter for the Seller," but this is not reflected in any mechanism. DL 5 is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- If the Company pays them post-Completion, we bear the cost.
- **Push back:** either (i) a specific Transaction Bonus line in the funds flow, deducted from the price, paid through Company payroll with withholding, and grossed up for triggered on-costs; or (ii) Seller funding at Completion, backed by an indemnity covering the bonuses and any on-costs.
- Ask the Seller to confirm the on-cost position. Do not assume any particular rate or amount.

**D4. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)**

- The Seller asserts these are ordinary-course costs. DL 8 says it does not state whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. DL 8 also says DD-008 and DD-011 should be read together.
- **Our position is to assess, not to assume either way.** Do not demand automatic Debt classification or a price deduction. Do not accept the "ordinary course" label without diligence either.
- **Action:** request contract terms, timing, termination rights, accrual treatment and whether the three renewals are linked or split. Then decide on Debt-like, working-capital or specific-indemnity treatment.

### E. Specific risk items

**E1. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)**

- The existing indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment, and the Seller calls it "adequate." DD-004 cl 7.3 ties transfer of SOW3 Project Materials to cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- The risk is therefore wider than a payment dispute. It extends to ownership of the deliverables and to third-party claims.
- **Push back:** broaden the indemnity to cover loss from any failure of title to or right to use the SOW3 Project Materials and any related claim, while **preserving the SOW3 cure** (payment plus a confirmatory assignment). Ideally make that cure a pre-Completion deliverable.
- The AUD 180,000 in DD-010 is not independently verified **in either direction**. Do not cite it as an established liability. Seek bank evidence and Ironquay confirmation.
- The indemnity must sit outside the general cap, basket and knowledge bar.

**E2. DD-006 export incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6)**

- The Seller calls it preliminary and not expected to be material. DL 6 confirms the investigation is preliminary, with access, scope and notification status unknown, ~1,240 records potentially involved, and no breach or loss characterised.
- **Our stance must be balanced.** We do not assert a confirmed breach, harm, a notification duty or any quantum. We equally do not accept "not material" as a conclusion. It is an assertion.
- **Push back:** require log preservation, a completed investigation (ideally by an independent forensic provider), regular written updates to the Buyer before Completion, Buyer consultation rights on any notification decision, and a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident, outside the general limitations.
- As the Seller's information is about six weeks old, request a current status update.

### F. Title

**F1. Title evidence (DL 10)**

- The Seller relies solely on the DD-012 share register. DL 10 itself concedes this is a source relied on and not Buyer verification. An internal register is not independent proof.
- **Require:** an ASIC company extract consistent with the register; original share certificates or evidence of uncertificated holding; constitution and any shareholder agreement (pre-emption and drag/tag waivers); a PPSR search against the Seller and the Company; confirmation of no options, convertibles or rights to issue shares; and Seller board authority and capacity evidence.
- The Riverlark security release is relevant here too, if the shares are encumbered.

### G. Lower-priority items: accept the disclosure, but verify

- **Office lease (DD-007):** notification only, no consent. Diligence should confirm there is no change-of-control termination or consent right elsewhere in the lease. Make giving the notice a Completion deliverable.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** the restriction is on assignment, not a share sale. Confirm there is no change-of-control clause. No CP is needed if confirmed.

---

## 3. Contradictions to raise with the Seller

| Seller cover note says | Seller Disclosure Letter says |
|---|---|
| Bluefen consent "addressed" | No final consent and no evidence of conditions satisfied (DL 2) |
| DD-006 "not expected to be material" | Investigation preliminary; access, scope and notification undetermined (DL 6) |
| Sandbar renewals are "ordinary course" | Letter does not state whether they are ordinary course (DL 8) |
| Title "evidenced" by DD-012 | DD-012 is the source relied on, not verification (DL 10) |
| Tax and IP "settled" | No such agreement exists on our side (playbook: OPEN) |
| Funds flow reflects "agreed price mechanics" | Bonuses do not appear in the funds flow (DL 5); price mechanics are not agreed |

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

**Reject and restate the playbook position:**
1. Cap: **25% / AUD 6.0m**. Do not concede 20%.
2. De minimis **AUD 5,000**. Basket **AUD 50,000, tipping**.
3. Claims period: **24 months**.
4. Delete the cl 12.3/13 catch-all. Limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims, and only where expressly stated.
5. Separate Title and Capacity regime: **100% cap, at least 6 years**, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
6. **Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out** from all limitations, exclusive-remedy, non-reliance and disclosure provisions. Non-negotiable.
7. Tax and IP: respond that these are **open**, not settled.
8. Delete general disclosure in DL 1.1 and 1.2. Specific fair disclosure only.
9. Delete the cl 8.3 buyer-knowledge bar.

**Completion and cash protections:**
10. Bluefen: a CP requiring effective consent **plus evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied**, with an obligation stronger than reasonable endeavours.
11. Riverlark: current payout letter, direct repayment in the funds flow, and executed releases at Completion.
12. Bonuses: AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a funds-flow line item or Seller-funded, with an indemnity.
13. Sandbar: diligence first. No automatic Debt treatment and no acceptance of the "ordinary course" label.

**Specific indemnities and diligence:**
14. Ironquay: broaden the indemnity to IP title and use, preserve the SOW3 cure, and verify payment status independently.
15. DD-006: preservation, investigation, updates and consultation, plus a specific indemnity. No assumptions of breach or quantum either way.
16. Title: independent evidence pack (ASIC, PPSR, certificates, constitution, authority).
17. Lease and Mossvale: confirm through diligence. Handle the lease notice as a Completion deliverable.

**Process points:**
- **No fallback (20% cap or 18 months) may be offered** unless Amelia Frost gives prior written authority identifying this draft. None has been given. If the team wants to use either fallback, seek that authority first. Even then, it should be assessed only together with the other limitation terms, not as an isolated number.
- **Refresh the facts.** The Disclosure Letter is dated 22 September 2026. Before the mark-up goes out, request updated status on Riverlark, Bluefen, DD-006, the Ironquay payment and the bonus conditions, and an updated data-room index. Distinguish verified updates from Seller assertions in our responses.
- **Do not treat Seller labels as settled.** Terms such as "agreed," "addressed," "settled," "adequate" or "ordinary course" are Seller assertions. Our mark-up and cover note should say expressly that nothing is agreed until the SPA is executed.

I can turn this into a mark-up cover note to the Seller's counsel, with the internal-only process points removed, or into a draft clause rider for the fraud carve-out and the separate Fundamental regime.
=== END ADVICE ===
